distractors: A permanent supporting layer that everything above it is built on.
An outer shell that hides how untidy the thing underneath actually is.
A worked reference version others copy from, kept current so that the copies stay close to it.
A staged rollout that widens from a handful of users to everyone, with a gate at each step. Nothing is taken away; the reach simply grows.
A checklist worked through at every stage of a project, where each item has to be signed before the next stage may open. It stays in force for the life of the work.
A wrapper that adapts one interface so it can be called as though it were another.
A set of recorded results kept as the baseline that later runs get compared against.
A monitoring layer that watches a live system and raises the alarm when a number moves outside its band. It reports; it never intervenes.
A gate in the release pipeline that holds a build back until every check on the list has come back green. It decides, and it measures nothing itself.
A masked copy of production data, refreshed on a schedule, so that people can work against something realistic without ever touching a real record.
A flag that keeps unfinished work hidden from users.
A rehearsal of the release performed end to end beforehand.
A separate account opened so that one team's spend shows on its own bill rather than everyone else's.
A staging environment that mirrors production closely and reads from the same live data as production does.
A record of everything the system did and who asked for it, kept untouched so an auditor can reconstruct any decision later.
